items.name: add-to-cart-button
items.title: Add To Cart Button
items.description: Add-to-cart button that sends a small paper price tag along an arc into the cart; the cart badge bumps like a stamp. Use on product cards and detail pages. Reduced motion skips the flight.

whenToUse: Product cards and quick-add rows in a shop
Any action that moves an item somewhere the user can see
watchOut: Point the flight at a cart icon that stays visible, or the motion has nowhere to land
Keep the server request independent of the animation so a slow network does not freeze it

items.name: addon-checklist
items.title: Add-on Checklist
items.description: A paper receipt of optional extras with dotted leaders between each item and its price, where every row is a checkbox and the subtotal rolls to its new value as you tick. Rows use role=checkbox with keyboard toggling, the subtotal is announced via aria-live, and the number jumps instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Gift wrap, warranty and accessory upsells on a product or cart page
Booking extras such as parking, prints or insurance before checkout
watchOut: The total is display only; recalculate the price on the server from the selected ids
Required rows always count toward the total and cannot be unticked

items.name: animated-number
items.title: Animated Number
items.description: Mechanical odometer for prices and counts: each digit wheel turns in the direction the value moved, with Intl currency formatting and an optional small ink trend arrow. Screen readers get the formatted value.

whenToUse: Prices, totals and counters that change after a choice
Dashboard stats that update live
watchOut: Use tabular numbers so the width does not jump
Do not animate numbers that change many times a second

items.name: announcement-strip
items.title: Announcement Strip
items.description: A paper strip notice bar for the top of the store with notched ends, manual previous and next for several messages, and a dismiss that collapses its height and is remembered under a storageKey. Messages sit in a labelled region with a polite live area, controls have ARIA labels, and the collapse is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Site-wide notices such as free shipping thresholds, holiday returns or store hours
Rotating two or three short messages in one bar without auto-playing
watchOut: With a storageKey the strip renders after mount, so reserve no space for it or accept a small shift; change the key when the message changes
Keep each message to one line on mobile; long copy wraps and makes the bar tall

items.name: avatar-stack
items.title: Avatar Stack
items.description: Recent buyers social proof: initials on paper discs with an ink outline, a +N count and hover or focus tooltips. Use near add-to-cart to show real purchase activity.

whenToUse: Showing collaborators on a document, project or channel
Compact team rows in cards and table cells
watchOut: Each avatar is a tab stop so tooltips work by keyboard; keep max low in dense tables
Initials colors come from the name, so two people with the same name share a color

items.name: bill-split-rows
items.title: Bill Split Rows
items.description: Paper rows for splitting a bill item by item: an editable name and tabular amount, toggle chips for who shared each item (with an All toggle and tiny identity dots), and a live hint like '3 people · about $3.33 each' plus who takes the leftover cent. Rows with no one picked or an invalid amount show inline problem text instead of blocking, and the footer checks the items total against the bill. Chips use aria-pressed, totals update via aria-live, and row add or remove is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Bill splitting apps where each dish is shared by different people
Group orders that need a per-item who-pays breakdown
watchOut: Pair it with settlement-receipt for the final result; this block only edits items
Amounts are split in the currency's minor unit, so leftover cents go to the first person sharing the item

items.name: capsule-nav
items.title: Capsule Nav
items.description: A centered floating pill navigation that gains a backing once you scroll past a small threshold, can tuck away while scrolling down and returns on scroll up (never while focus is inside), and highlights the current section via IntersectionObserver with a sliding active pill. On mobile it collapses to the logo and a menu button whose sheet traps focus, closes on Escape and locks scrolling. Links carry aria-current=location, scrolling is rAF throttled, and smooth scrolling and pill motion become instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Landing and product pages with a handful of in-page sections
Docs or long-form pages that need a compact, always reachable nav
watchOut: Give each section the same id as its nav item or the active pill never moves
Pass scrollContainer when the page scrolls inside an element instead of the window

items.name: chapter-seekbar
items.title: Chapter Seekbar
items.description: A media seek bar that draws chapters as separate segments with small gaps, swells on hover with the hovered chapter tallest, and shows a time chip with the chapter or marker name. Markers snap clicks to their time. Dragging uses pointer capture and writes positions straight to the DOM, and it shows the buffered range. It is a role=slider with arrow keys for 5 seconds, PageUp/PageDown for chapters, Home/End, and an aria-valuetext naming the time and chapter; the swell is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Course and tutorial video players with named chapters
Podcast or long recording players where listeners jump between sections
watchOut: Pause playback in onScrubStart and resume in onScrubEnd so time updates do not fight the drag
Keep chapter starts sorted and inside the duration

items.name: checkin-streak
items.title: Check-in Streak
items.description: A seven-day check-in card showing done, missed, today and upcoming days with their point rewards, a streak count and a points total. Checking in calls an async onCheckIn with checking and retry states, then presses a vermilion stamp into today's circle. The reward is announced via aria-live, and under reduced motion the stamp appears instantly.

whenToUse: Daily login rewards in shop apps and member centers
Loyalty programs that pay points for coming back
watchOut: Compute todayIndex and checked days on the server in the shopper's time zone
Make onCheckIn idempotent so a double tap does not grant points twice

items.name: checkout-steps
items.title: Checkout Steps
items.description: A checkout progress indicator built on a semantic ordered list: completed steps draw a check and can jump back when onStepClick is given, the current step carries aria-current="step", and connectors fill with the theme primary as steps complete. Below the sm breakpoint it collapses to a single 'Step 2 of 4' row with a segmented bar; with reduced motion the fills and checks switch instantly.

whenToUse: Multi page or multi section checkout flows
Any short linear wizard where users may go back to edit an earlier step
watchOut: Keep it to five steps or fewer so labels fit on one row
Only let users jump back to completed steps, never skip ahead

items.name: choice-cards
items.title: Choice Cards
items.description: A radio group of equal-height paper cards for picking a delivery method, bundle or plan, where each card spells out its gains, its trade-offs and what it includes automatically. The selected card gets an ink border and lifts slightly, and a line below explains what the choice means. It is a proper radiogroup with roving tabindex, arrow, Home/End and digit-key selection; disabled cards state their reason, the explanation is announced via aria-live, and the lift is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Delivery, bundle or plan choices where each option has real trade-offs
Onboarding picks where users should see what a choice turns on before committing
watchOut: Keep it to four options or fewer; more cards stop being comparable
Write costs honestly; hiding the downside defeats the point of the layout

items.name: cjk-heading
items.title: CJK Heading
items.description: Typeset Traditional Chinese and Japanese campaign headlines: punctuation compression, CJK and Latin spacing, optional vertical writing and a vermilion seal highlight for one key word. No motion.

whenToUse: Chinese or Japanese headlines on landing pages
Editorial layouts that want vertical writing
watchOut: Vertical writing needs a fixed height and short lines
Check punctuation placement in every target font

items.name: compare-slider
items.title: Compare Slider
items.description: A before/after comparison where a transparent native range input on top drives the divider, so click-to-jump, arrow keys, Home/End and screen readers all work, with aria-valuetext reading the before and after percentages. The after layer is revealed with clip-path, the paper grip moves by transform, and an opt-in one-time demo sweep plays on first view, stops on any interaction and is skipped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Product pages showing wear, patina or before and after care
Print proofs, retouching or restoration results
watchOut: Both layers must share the same framing or the comparison misleads
Keep demoSweep for one hero instance; several sweeping at once is noise

items.name: confirm-button
items.title: Confirm Button
items.description: A two-press button for light destructive actions that replaces confirm dialogs: the first press arms it and swaps the label to the outcome (e.g. Press again to remove) while a hairline drains over the confirm window, and a second press within that window runs an async onConfirm with busy, error and done states. Escape, blur or timeout disarm it; the instruction is wired through aria-describedby, results are announced via aria-live, and label swaps are instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Removing saved addresses, payment methods or list items without opening a dialog
Cancelling an order or subscription where an accidental single click must not count
watchOut: Write armedLabel as the outcome, not a generic OK, so the second press is unambiguous
For actions that can be held back a few seconds, prefer undo-toast over asking twice

items.name: content-gate
items.title: Content Gate
items.description: Gates paid content after the first free items (or a preview height) with an opaque paper panel that overlaps the locked content along a perforated tear line, no blur or gradient. Copy differs for signed-out shoppers and members without access, with a vermilion price, primary and secondary actions, and a Later button that collapses the panel to a slim reminder bar. Locked content is inert and aria-hidden, unlocking expands it with a spring and is announced via aria-live, and reduced motion makes it instant.

whenToUse: Courses, guides or articles with a free preview and a paid remainder
Member-only sections inside an otherwise public page
watchOut: Gate on the server too; locked content is still in the DOM and only hidden from the UI
In previewHeight mode the whole content is inert while locked, so put the free summary outside the gate

items.name: copy-code-button
items.title: Copy Code Button
items.description: Printed promo code slip with a dashed outline; copying presses a small vermilion COPIED stamp and announces the result. Falls back when the clipboard API is unavailable.

whenToUse: Coupon and promo codes in checkout or emails
Any short string the user needs to paste elsewhere
watchOut: Clipboard access needs a secure context (https or localhost)
Keep the code visible as text so it can still be copied by hand

items.name: countdown-banner
items.title: Countdown Banner
items.description: Paper sale banner with discount, prices and a printed flip-card countdown to a real end date; shows an ended stamp when time is up. Supports English and Chinese copy.

whenToUse: Time limited sales with a real end time
Launch day announcements
watchOut: Only show a countdown that reflects a real deadline
Render the end time on the server so every visitor sees the same clock

items.name: coupon-wallet
items.title: Coupon Wallet
items.description: A stack of owned coupons that fans out on hover, keyboard focus or a first tap, so shoppers can compare and pick one to apply, which stamps it Applied. It is a radiogroup with roving focus (arrow keys, Home, End, Escape to collapse), ineligible coupons explain why in their label, and the fan snaps into place without motion under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Choosing which of several owned coupons to apply at checkout or in the cart
A compact coupon picker where a full list would push the order summary off screen
watchOut: The fan is about 1.5 card widths wide, so give it a column of at least 22rem or keep it to four coupons
Recalculate the discount on the server; the selection only tells you which coupon the shopper picked

items.name: dialogue-box
items.title: Dialogue Box
items.description: A visual novel dialogue box with a narration style that floats without a box and a dialogue style with an accent-bordered speaker plate. Text types out at a set characters-per-second rate: the first click, Enter or Space completes the line and the next one advances, while a breathing next glyph stays attached to the last character so it never wraps alone. An optional autoplay ring drains before advancing, and choice mode shows numbered choices (digit keys pick them) with locked choices tagged by their requirement. Screen readers get each whole line once via aria-live, colours come from --story-* variables, and reduced motion shows full text with a still glyph.

whenToUse: Visual novels, interactive fiction and narrative game scenes
Onboarding or product tours told as a short scripted conversation
watchOut: Change the text prop for each new line; the typewriter restarts whenever the text changes
Digit-key shortcuts listen on the window while choices are shown, so avoid two choice boxes on one page at once

items.name: dot-badge
items.title: Dot Badge
items.description: Status and people chips where colour lives only on a 6px dot and the text stays ink, so a column of statuses never turns into a rainbow. Ships StatusDot, DotBadge (with a screen-reader hint), PersonChip (CJK-aware initials, deterministic low-chroma hue per person, aria-pressed toggle with inverted ink, muted and locked states) plus initialOf and personHue helpers. Only the live tone breathes, and it stays still under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Order, payment and fulfilment status columns in admin tables
Staff or member filters where each person needs a stable, recognisable mark
watchOut: Keep the label text meaningful on its own; the dot colour is a supplement, not the message
Use the live tone only for things actually in progress, or the breathing loses its meaning

items.name: expanding-search
items.title: Expanding Search
items.description: Store search field that expands into a paper slip of product suggestions with thumbnails, prices and keyboard navigation (combobox pattern, / shortcut).

whenToUse: Compact navbars where a full search field does not fit
Sites where search is secondary but should stay one click away
watchOut: Leave room in the layout for the expanded width so neighbouring items do not jump
Built-in filtering is a simple substring match; set filterSuggestions to false for server results

items.name: explain-panel
items.title: Explain Panel
items.description: Review AI or solver suggestions with the reasons behind them: each card lists what changes and where, met, caveat and conflict reasons, a confidence bar and the impact, with Accept and Reject that collapse it to a one-line receipt with Undo. A header counts accepted items and offers Accept safe ones, which never includes suggestions marked for review, plus Reject all; an optional candidate list adds Pick actions. Reason glyphs carry screen-reader prefixes, decisions are announced via aria-live, and transitions are instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Applying AI cleanup or auto-scheduling suggestions only after a person reviews them
Explaining why a solver picked one candidate over others
watchOut: Mark anything that changes orders, money or length as needsReview so bulk accept skips it
Write reasons as checkable facts, not marketing copy, or the confidence number means nothing

items.name: favorite-button
items.title: Favorite Button
items.description: Wishlist heart in ink that fills vermilion with a stamp-like press when saved. aria-pressed toggle with optional count.

whenToUse: Wishlists, likes and saves on product or content cards
Lightweight toggles that deserve a little delight
watchOut: Update the count optimistically and roll back on error
Give it an accessible name that includes the item

items.name: hold-to-redeem
items.title: Hold To Redeem
items.description: A press-and-hold button for irreversible spends such as redeeming points: a fill grows linearly while held (pointer or Space/Enter), rewinds with a hint if released early, then calls an async onConfirm and turns into a paper voucher line with a vermilion Redeemed stamp and optional code. The hold instruction is wired through aria-describedby and the result is announced via aria-live; under reduced motion the rewind and stamp are instant while the time-based fill still shows progress.

whenToUse: Redeeming points, vouchers or one-time rewards that can't be undone
Any spend where an accidental tap would cost the shopper something
watchOut: Keep holdMs around one second; longer holds feel broken, not safe
Use it only for irreversible actions, or it becomes friction on ordinary buttons

items.name: honest-countdown
items.title: Honest Countdown
items.description: A sale or launch countdown that never hides the real deadline: the server renders only the absolute end date in a time element, then the browser adds day, hour and minute tiles, with seconds only inside the final hour and digits turning vermilion in that hour. It stops ticking while the tab is hidden and resyncs on return, and on expiry calls onEnd once and presses an ink Ended stamp. The tiles are a role=timer group with a spoken label, only the end is announced, and digit changes are instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Sale, launch or registration deadlines that are real
Campaign pages where shoppers need the exact end time
watchOut: Pass a timeZone when the deadline is tied to one region, or the absolute date follows the viewer's zone
Never reset the target on reload to fake urgency

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: A product quick-view card that opens after a short hover delay and stays open while the pointer moves into it, with price, discount and an add to cart button on paper. Keyboard focus opens it, Escape closes it and returns focus, touch opens it on first tap, it flips above the trigger near the viewport edge, and reduced motion removes the slide.

whenToUse: Product names inside carts, bundles or editorial text where a quick preview saves a page visit
Recommendation lists where shoppers compare price before opening the product page
watchOut: It is positioned inside its parent, so an overflow hidden ancestor will clip the card
Keep essential information on the product page too; the card is a shortcut, not the only place

items.name: job-progress
items.title: Job Progress
items.description: A paper work-order slip for long jobs such as custom prints, AI generation or exports: named steps with checks, a non-linear progress bar from the exported jobPercent helper (queued 2%, steps 15 to 95, finishing 97, done 100), queue position, ETA and an honest reason line for slow paths, with Cancel, Retry and a vermilion Done stamp plus result action. A compact single-line row variant suits job lists; only state and step changes are announced via aria-live, and the bar and stamp are instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Print-on-demand, personalization or AI generation orders that take minutes
Export or render queues where users can leave and come back
watchOut: Drive status from your real job record; never animate fake progress
Give a reason line when a job takes the slow path so users don't think it is stuck

items.name: jobs-tray
items.title: Jobs Tray
items.description: A bottom-right stack of named background jobs that replaces blocking full-screen overlays: running jobs show a progress bar and percent, finished ones collapse on their own after a few seconds, and failed ones stay with the reason plus Retry and Dismiss. A collapsible header summarises '3 tasks · 1 failed', the tray takes no space when empty, and a useJobs hook manages the list. Only completions and failures are announced via aria-live, and slides become instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Exports, imports and bulk edits that run while the user keeps working
Replacing full-screen 'please wait' overlays in admin tools
watchOut: Keep failed jobs until the user dismisses them; silent failures are worse than slow ones
Give each job a label that still makes sense out of context, like 'Export orders.csv'

items.name: karaoke-caption
items.title: Karaoke Caption
items.description: Time-synced captions that highlight as speech plays: Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is timed per character and Latin text per word, with spoken words in full colour, the current one in the accent and upcoming ones dimmed. The font size steps down for long lines, and a useMediaTime hook reads the time from an audio or video element. Screen readers hear each cue once rather than per word, colour changes are instant under reduced motion, and all colours come from --story-* theme variables.

whenToUse: Product voiceovers, narrated stories and short videos with burned-in style captions
Language learning or read-along pages that follow audio
watchOut: Cue start and end times must match the audio; the per-word timing inside a cue is only an estimate
Keep cues to one or two short lines, or the plate covers too much of the video

items.name: live-bento
items.title: Live Bento
items.description: A bento grid of feature tiles with 1x1, 2x1, 1x2 and 2x2 spans, where every tile's mini visual runs off one shared useTicker beat instead of separate timers. The beat stops when the grid leaves the viewport or the tab is hidden, and under reduced motion it stays at tick 0 so every tile shows a still frame. The visuals are decorative and hidden from screen readers; each tile's title and body carry the content.

whenToUse: Feature overviews on SaaS landing pages
Showing several small product behaviours side by side
watchOut: Choose spans that fill the 4-column grid, or desktop leaves holes
Draw a complete frame at tick 0, since reduced motion never advances past it

items.name: low-stock-indicator
items.title: Low Stock Indicator
items.description: Honest printed stock tag: one slip per unit when stock is small, otherwise a thin ink line; vermilion only at the critical level and a stamp when sold out. Never counts down on its own.

whenToUse: Product pages where stock is genuinely limited
Ticket and seat selection
watchOut: Only show real inventory numbers, fake scarcity erodes trust
Hide it entirely when stock is comfortable

items.name: media-picker
items.title: Media Picker
items.description: An inline panel for picking which images and videos of a post to download: a thumbnail grid with numbered badges in pick order, duration chips on videos, select all or none, a remembered 'Include caption text' option, and locked Pro options shown with their reason. The button reads 'Download file' for one pick and 'Download 3 as ZIP' for several. The grid is a multi-select listbox with arrow keys and Space, the summary is announced via aria-live, and badges switch instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Downloading or exporting selected media from a post, album or message
Choosing which attachments to share or archive
watchOut: Give each item meaningful alt text; the grid has no visible captions
Download a single pick directly instead of zipping one file

items.name: notice-queue
items.title: Notice Queue
items.description: A first-in-first-out queue of story notices (clue, item, bond, stat) that shows one single-line notice at a time in the top-right of its container, wiping in like ink and retracting to the left after 4.2 seconds. The timer pauses on hover, focus and while the tab is hidden, Escape dismisses the current notice and clicking opens it; a useNoticeQueue hook manages push and dismiss. Each notice is announced once via aria-live, all colours come from --story-* variables with ink, rice and moon themes, and the wipe becomes a plain fade under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Narrative games and interactive fiction that award clues, items or relationship changes
Any story reader that needs quiet, one-at-a-time feedback without covering the text
watchOut: Keep titles to one short line; long text is truncated
Escape is listened to on the window, so stop it from bubbling if a modal also uses Escape

items.name: order-history
items.title: Order History
items.description: A receipt-style list of past orders with small status stamps, expandable line items with dotted leaders and totals, an actions slot for buy again or track, and an empty state. Each row is a disclosure button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the expand and collapse are instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: The orders tab of a customer account page
A recent orders panel on an account dashboard with buy again shortcuts
watchOut: Totals are computed from line items, shipping and discount on the client; pass server-confirmed values so they match the real charge
For a single order's shipping timeline use order-tracker instead

items.name: otp-input
items.title: OTP Input
items.description: One-time code entry styled like boxes on a printed form: auto-advance, paste to fill, keyboard navigation, a short error shake and a VERIFIED stamp.

whenToUse: Sign in and two step verification codes
Short numeric codes from SMS or email
watchOut: Keep autocomplete one-time-code so phones can autofill
Do not auto-submit before the last digit is entered

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: Page navigation with a fixed width ellipsis range (first, last, current and siblings), previous and next controls, aria-current="page" and an optional compact '3 / 12' mode; pass getHref to render crawlable links or onPageChange for buttons. A small underline slides to the current page with a snappy spring, and jumps instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Product listing, search result and order history pages with a known page count
SEO sensitive catalogues where every page needs a real link
watchOut: Use getHref for pages that should be indexed; buttons alone are invisible to crawlers
For endless feeds without a total count, prefer a load more button

items.name: pause-menu
items.title: Pause Menu
items.description: An in-stage pause panel for story games: an objective line, a vertical menu whose focused row gets an accent light bar that sweeps in from the left, a quick load that needs a second press within 2.5 seconds, and an honest two-step exit that says exactly what will be lost since the last save and offers Save and exit, Exit without saving or Back. Arrow keys, Home/End and Esc work, focus is trapped in the dialog and returned on close, and under reduced motion the bar and nudge switch instantly. All colours come from --story-* variables, so ink, rice and moon themes reskin it.

whenToUse: Pause and exit flows in narrative or visual novel style web games
Any in-app session where leaving can lose unsaved progress
watchOut: Place it inside a position: relative stage; it covers its parent, not the viewport
Pass lastSave so the exit warning can say what will actually be lost

items.name: payment-status-banner
items.title: Payment Status Banner
items.description: A paper receipt banner for the page shoppers land on after an external payment redirect. While pending it polls a check() function on an interval, pausing while the tab is hidden, then turns paid with a vermilion stamp, failed with a retry, or an honest timeout with a Check again button. Status changes are announced via aria-live, and under reduced motion the stamp and text swaps are instant.

whenToUse: Order confirmation pages after Stripe, PayPal or bank redirects
Any purchase where the webhook can arrive after the shopper returns
watchOut: check() should read your own order record, not trust URL query params
Keep the timeout copy honest so shoppers do not pay twice

items.name: preflight-checklist
items.title: Preflight Checklist
items.description: Shows readiness checks and permissions right next to the main call to action instead of in a dialog: each row has a severity dot, a message and an inline fix, and a summary line says whether anything blocks. The CTA stays disabled only while a blocking check or required permission is unresolved, and then explains which fix comes first via aria-describedby. Rows can be rechecked with a per-row spinner, the summary is a polite live region, and the spinner stays still under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Go-live, publish or record screens that depend on devices, permissions or storage
First-run setup where the user should see everything that is missing in one place
watchOut: Only use block for problems that really stop the action; warnings should never disable the CTA
Give every non-ok row a concrete fix action instead of telling the user to look elsewhere

items.name: print-preview
items.title: Print Preview
items.description: Lays a list of blocks such as invoice headers, line item groups and totals onto stacked A4 or Letter paper pages, splitting pages only between blocks so no block is ever cut, and giving any block taller than a page its own page. Pages scale to the container width, carry an optional header and a Page 1 of 2 footer, and include print CSS that maps each preview page to a real printed page with the rest of the site hidden.

whenToUse: Invoice, receipt and packing slip previews before printing
Order or report pages that must print cleanly without split rows
watchOut: Split long tables into several child blocks; one giant block cannot be paginated
Children render twice, once hidden for measuring, so keep them free of side effects

items.name: quantity-stepper
items.title: Quantity Stepper
items.description: Receipt-style quantity stepper with tabular count, long-press repeat, typed input, min and max limits and a remove action at the minimum.

whenToUse: Cart and checkout line items
Any bounded numeric input changed in small steps
watchOut: The plus and minus buttons are removed from the tab order; keyboard users adjust via the field itself
Typed values snap to the nearest step, so tell users when step is larger than 1

items.name: quota-meter
items.title: Quota Meter
items.description: A paper usage meter that talks in outcomes, not points: 'About 42 photos left' from the remaining credits and cost per unit, a hairline bar, percent used and the reset date. An optional nudge such as an unclaimed check-in replaces the second line, and the remaining number turns vermilion when credits run low. Comes as a card or a compact header pill; the bar is a labelled meter and its fill is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Credit based AI tools and plans with monthly allowances
Headers that show how much of a quota is left at a glance
watchOut: Refetch used and total after each job so the estimate stays honest
Pick a unitLabel the shopper understands, never raw credits

items.name: recording-hud
items.title: Recording HUD
items.description: A draggable floating pill for screen or audio recording with a blinking red rec dot that turns amber when paused, a mono elapsed timer written straight to the DOM, pause, stop and a draw tool that pops a pen colour row with Clear. Dragging uses pointer capture and stays inside the parent or viewport. It is a labelled toolbar where Space toggles pause when focused, and the dot holds steady under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Screen recorders, walkthrough tools and voice memo apps
Any long capture where users need pause and stop without leaving the screen
watchOut: Pass elapsed from your recorder clock so pauses are exact; startedAt alone cannot know about pauses
Keep it out of the recorded area or exclude it from capture

items.name: redeem-key-input
items.title: Redeem Key Input
items.description: A printed-voucher card for redeeming gift cards, license keys and promo codes: the mono input uppercases, strips stray characters and groups the code with dashes as you type or paste, optionally detects the key type, and shows server errors inline. On success the field becomes the printed code with a vermilion Redeemed stamp; results are announced via aria-live and the stamp appears instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Account pages where customers redeem gift cards or store credit
Activating a license or supporter key in an app
watchOut: Throw an Error with an actionable message from onRedeem; the message is shown as is
Match length and groupSize to your real code format or valid codes cannot be completed

items.name: reservation-timer
items.title: Reservation Timer
items.description: A paper slip that shows how long a limited item or ticket is held for you, with a mono countdown, a hairline bar for the remaining hold and a slot for the item summary. It renders a placeholder until mounted, resyncs with real time when the tab returns, turns vermilion inside the warning window, and on expiry calls onExpire, fades and presses an ink Released stamp with an optional Hold again action. Screen readers hear only the warning crossing and the expiry, and reduced motion skips the stamp animation.

whenToUse: Ticket, seat or limited drop checkouts that hold stock for a few minutes
Cart sidebars where an item is reserved until payment
watchOut: Only show a hold the server actually enforces; never fake urgency
Release the stock on the server too, the onExpire callback is only the UI side

items.name: scan-report
items.title: Scan Report
items.description: A report view for code, accessibility or SEO scans: a 0 to 100 health score with a reason line, severity chips whose colour lives only on a dot and that toggle a filter, and issue cards that expand into a line-numbered code excerpt with the problem lines highlighted plus a fix with steps, difficulty, ETA and a copyable before and after. Chips use aria-pressed, the issue count is a polite live region, and the expand animation is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Accessibility, performance or code quality scan results
Audit pages where each finding needs location, evidence and a fix
watchOut: Explain the score in scoreReason, a bare number gives no next step
Keep excerpts short; the highlight range should point at the exact lines to change

items.name: schedule-grid
items.title: Schedule Grid
items.description: A weekly staff schedule with shifts as rows and days as columns, a sticky shift column, person chips whose colour lives only on a dot, dashed amber Short N buttons on understaffed cells, amber outlines on cells changed since the last version, and a focus mode that fades everyone but one person. It renders a real table with th scopes and aria-current on today, selection uses aria-pressed, and below md it becomes a snap-scrolling one-day-per-view strip with dot navigation.

whenToUse: Shift planning for shops, cafes and clinics
Any week view where gaps and changes must stand out at a glance
watchOut: Keys for required and changedKeys are day:row, keep ids stable
Keep row colours as identity marks only, never as status

items.name: scripted-demo
items.title: Scripted Demo
items.description: A landing-page product demo that plays fake-UI scenes on timers, grouped into chapter tabs whose progress bars fill as each chapter runs; a fake cursor glides to each scene's data-demo-target element and shows a click ripple. It only plays while in view and while the tab is visible, has a play, pause and replay button, and lets you click a chapter to jump. The mock stage is inert so keyboard focus skips it; under reduced motion nothing auto-advances and the button steps through static scenes.

whenToUse: Landing page heroes that show the product working without a video
Feature pages that walk through a short flow in chapters
watchOut: Give each scene's target a data-demo-target attribute or the cursor hides for that scene
Keep the whole loop under about 15 seconds; longer demos lose people before the payoff

items.name: scroll-progress
items.title: Scroll Progress
items.description: Hairline ink reading progress rule for the window or a scroll container, with optional section ticks you can jump to.

whenToUse: Long articles, docs and changelogs
Step based onboarding pages
watchOut: Hide it on short pages where it adds noise
Section markers need stable heading ids

items.name: scroll-reveal-text
items.title: Scroll Reveal Text
items.description: Paragraph whose characters (CJK) or words (Latin) darken from faint to full ink as the reader scrolls. Accent phrases can print in vermilion.

whenToUse: Manifesto or mission statements on landing pages
Story style product sections
watchOut: Keep the full text readable without scrolling for screen readers
Long paragraphs feel slow, use it on two to four lines

items.name: scroll-story
items.title: Scroll Story
items.description: A feature story with text steps on the left and a sticky visual stage on the right, where an IntersectionObserver on the viewport's center line picks the active step and only that step's visual is mounted and animating. On mobile, and on the server before mount, each step renders its visual inline under its text and plays once when scrolled into view. Steps expose aria-current and a spoken step count, the stage is decorative and hidden from screen readers, and reduced motion renders every visual in its final frame.

whenToUse: Explaining a process in 3 to 5 steps on a landing or help page
How-it-works sections where each step has its own illustration
watchOut: visual(false) must draw the finished frame because the server, mobile and reduced motion all use it
Keep the important information in the step text; the stage is decorative and hidden from screen readers

items.name: seeded-cover
items.title: Seeded Cover
items.description: A zero-asset placeholder cover for products, books and courses without images: the seed picks a low-chroma paper tint and a thin SVG line, dot or grid texture, so the same item always gets the same cover in light and dark. Chinese titles on book-shaped covers set vertically in a serif, everything else sets horizontally with a subtitle and an optional corner label. Rendered as role=img with the title as its accessible name; it has no motion.

whenToUse: Catalog items, ebooks or courses that have no cover image yet
Seed data and empty storefronts that should still look intentional
watchOut: Use a stable id as the seed, not the title, so renaming does not repaint the cover
Replace it with real product photos once they exist; it is a placeholder, not branding

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: Segmented Control
items.description: Product variant picker: sizes or colors as typographic chips with one shared ink outline that slides between them, sold-out options struck through. Radio group semantics.

whenToUse: Switching between 2 to 5 mutually exclusive views or ranges
Compact filters like Daily, Weekly, Monthly or list and grid view
watchOut: Too many or long labels overflow; use tabs or a select instead
Icon-only options need a string label or ariaLabel for screen readers

items.name: sensitive-image
items.title: Sensitive Image
items.description: An image that is covered by an opaque paper panel from the very first frame when flagged, so the original never flashes, with a rating chip, a one-line reason and a Show button that reveals it for this view only. The alt text stays neutral until revealed, the Show button is never nested inside the image button, and the reveal fades gently or instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Customer photo reviews that may contain spoilers or graphic content
User uploaded images that need a content rating before display
watchOut: Flag on the server so the cover is in the first render
Do not persist the reveal unless users explicitly opt in

items.name: settlement-receipt
items.title: Settlement Receipt
items.description: A torn-edge paper receipt for split bills: per-person subtotals with a line breakdown and payer tag, a balance check against the bill total, and a transfer list where each row is a checkbox to mark as sent. When every transfer is ticked a vermilion Settled stamp presses on, and a Copy summary button copies a plain-text recap. Settling is announced via aria-live and the stamp is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Bill splitting and group order results
Showing who owes whom after a shared purchase
watchOut: Pass the real bill total so mismatches surface instead of hiding rounding errors
Transfers reference people by id; unknown ids fall back to the raw id

items.name: shipping-options
items.title: Shipping Options
items.description: Ticket-stub radio cards for delivery methods: a perforated stub holds the method name and radio dot, the body shows the arrival date, note and fee, and free shipping is printed in vermilion. Works as a radiogroup with arrow keys and roving focus, skips disabled methods, wraps to a single column on narrow screens, and the dot switches instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Choosing standard, express or pickup delivery at checkout
Any single choice between two to five priced options with a date
watchOut: Recalculate the shipping fee on the server; the card fee is display only
Mark unavailable methods as disabled instead of hiding them so shoppers know why

items.name: side-panel
items.title: Side Panel
items.description: Paper sheet drawer from the left, right or bottom over a flat ink scrim, with focus trap, Escape to close, scroll lock and focus return.

whenToUse: Filters, carts and detail views beside a list
Mobile navigation and settings
watchOut: Trap focus and restore it to the trigger on close
Avoid stacking more than one drawer

items.name: skeleton-set
items.title: Skeleton Set
items.description: Paper placeholders for product cards, lists and text with a slow opacity pulse while loading, crossfading to real content. Sets aria-busy and announces when loaded.

whenToUse: First load of cards, lists and profiles
Any content that takes over 300 ms to arrive
watchOut: Match the real layout so the page does not jump
Use a spinner instead for actions under a second

items.name: speed-reader
items.title: Speed Reader
items.description: An RSVP reader that flashes one word at a time at a set words per minute, aligned on a highlighted recognition letter, pausing longer on punctuation and chunking Chinese or Japanese into two to three character groups. It has play and pause, skip back or forward ten words, a WPM stepper, a scrubbable progress slider, elapsed and remaining time, a context strip, an optional symbol filter and a shortcut sheet. Shortcuts only work while the reader has focus, it pauses when the tab is hidden, the paused position is announced via aria-live, and there is no animation beyond instant word swaps.

whenToUse: Blog or course pages that offer a fast-read mode
Reading practice and accessibility tools
watchOut: Keep the full text available elsewhere on the page; RSVP hides context
Remount with a key when the text changes, so reading restarts from the first word

items.name: star-rating
items.title: Star Rating
items.description: Ink star rating with half stars, keyboard roving focus, optional clear and a hidden form input; read-only mode for review summaries.

whenToUse: Collecting product or order reviews
Showing an average rating next to a review count
watchOut: Half-star hit areas are small on mobile; use precision 1 on touch-first forms
Pass a name prop if the value must be submitted with a native form

items.name: state-panels
items.title: State Panels
items.description: Three companion panels for empty, error and loading states. EmptyState offers a primary action plus a Load an example link. ErrorState never shows raw exceptions, tucks technical detail into a collapsible section and retries with a pending state. LoadingState draws static skeleton rows that match the real layout and adds a still-loading note after a delay. Errors use role=alert, loading is an aria-busy polite status, and there are no looping animations.

whenToUse: Order, return or invoice lists that can be empty, fail or load slowly
Any data panel that needs consistent empty, error and loading states
watchOut: Match the skeleton row count to the real content so it doesn't jump when it loads
Put request IDs in detail, never raw stack traces

items.name: story-player
items.title: Story Player
items.description: A full-bleed story viewer with segmented progress bars driven by requestAnimationFrame. Tap the left third to go back and elsewhere to go forward, press and hold to pause, and per-slide durations let closing slides linger. Slides move with direction-aware transitions and end on a screen of staggered actions plus replay. It is a focusable region with arrow-key and Space control, a pause button and polite slide announcements; it pauses when off screen or the tab is hidden, and under reduced motion it only crossfades and does not auto-advance unless autoPlay is set.

whenToUse: Year-in-review or monthly recap screens for shops and creators
Short onboarding or product tours told as a sequence of cards
watchOut: Keep each slide readable within its duration, and give dense slides a longer duration
Do not hide essential information inside a story; offer a plain page as well

items.name: terms-consent
items.title: Terms Consent
items.description: A paper slip of checkout consents where required items show an n / m counter and gate the pay button, while optional opt-ins like marketing email default to off. The button stays focusable with aria-disabled and explains why it is blocked through aria-describedby and a polite live region; with reduced motion the check marks switch instantly.

whenToUse: Right above the pay button when terms of sale or a privacy notice must be accepted
Sign up or subscription flows that mix required agreements with optional opt-ins
watchOut: The gate is only a UI hint, so record and verify consent on the server
Never pre-tick optional marketing items; many regions require an explicit opt-in

items.name: tier-progress
items.title: Tier Progress
items.description: A membership card with a half ring gauge showing points toward the next tier, a tier ladder and the perks the next tier unlocks, with a stamp once the top tier is reached. The gauge is a labelled progressbar with readable value text, SVG ids come from useId, and the arc moves only when points change, instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Account or rewards pages that show how far a member is from the next tier
Order confirmation pages that show the points just earned against the next tier
watchOut: Pass tiers sorted from lowest to highest threshold, with the first tier starting at 0

items.name: toast-stack
items.title: Toast Stack
items.description: Paper slip notifications that stack, fan out on hover or focus and dismiss by swipe or Escape, with optional product thumbnail and undo action. Includes a useToasts hook.

whenToUse: Confirmations after save, copy or add to cart
Non blocking errors that the user can retry
watchOut: Do not put critical errors only in a toast
Keep messages short and give actions a clear label

items.name: typewriter
items.title: Typewriter
items.description: Types phrases once with grapheme-correct CJK timing and rests on the last one (loop optional). Thin ink caret; screen readers get the full text once.

whenToUse: Hero headlines that rotate through use cases
Terminal or chat style intros
watchOut: Keep the static part of the sentence meaningful on its own
Respect reduced motion by showing the first phrase

items.name: undo-toast
items.title: Undo Toast
items.description: Replaces confirm dialogs with undo: a useUndo hook keeps one pending action and commits the previous one when a new one starts, and UndoToast shows a paper slip with an Undo button and a hairline that runs out over the duration, then commits. The timer pauses on hover, focus or when the tab is hidden; Escape commits, Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes (except while typing in a field), and the slip lives in an aria-live polite status region with instant transitions under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Removing cart items, saved addresses or wishlist entries without a confirm dialog
Any destructive action you can hold back for a few seconds before committing
watchOut: Apply the change optimistically in the UI and only call the server in onCommit
Don't use it for actions that can't be held back, such as payments

items.name: variant-picker
items.title: Variant Picker
items.description: Product colour swatches and size chips driven by per-combination stock, where sold-out sizes carry a faded ink Sold out stamp and cannot be picked, and the chosen colour name and remaining stock are shown below. Both rows are labelled radiogroups with arrow keys, swatch names live in aria-label, stock changes are announced politely, and press feedback is skipped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Apparel and goods product pages with colour and size variants
Showing low stock and sold-out combinations before add to cart
watchOut: Stock keys are colorId:sizeId and missing keys count as sold out
Switching to a colour where the chosen size is sold out clears the size

items.name: window-frame
items.title: Window Frame
items.description: A presentation frame for screenshots and live demos in mac, browser and phone variants, with neutral outline dots instead of colored traffic lights, a mono title or address bar, a right slot and a content area that scrolls inside a fixed height. Demo state is shown only through a 1px tone border plus an optional caption icon, and the frame is a figure with figcaption for assistive tech.

whenToUse: Landing and docs sections that show your store or app in context
Side by side desktop and mobile previews
watchOut: Use tone only for real demo states such as passed or failed, not decoration
Set height when content is long so the page does not jump
